body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#786, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: GitHub #705, #685 (appmap di_constants re-export reading); V1-1131 (#773 router dialects).

## Problem
On an adopter AngularJS/Angular hybrid app, `di_constants` scoped to the registering file still leaves the table unresolved. The result is 153 states `non-literal-name` and only 10 of 23 screens resolved, with one `di-constant` unknown `not-read-whole`. The shape:

```ts
// core-downgrade.module.ts (in di_constants scope)
import { RoutesConstants } from './routes'          // directory import -> routes/index.ts
...
.constant('StateConstants', RoutesConstants)

// routes/index.ts
export * from './routes.constants'

// routes/routes.constants.ts
export enum RoutesConstants { CLUB = 'app.club', TEESHEETS = 'app.club.teesheets', ... }  // every member a literal string
```

The #705 fix reads one level of `export ... from` behind the registering file's import, but apparently not when:
- the import specifier is a directory that resolves to `index.ts`; or
- the re-export is a star export (`export * from`) rather than a named `export { X } from`.

The same shape appears in a second app in the same repository (`not-read-whole`, 65 `non-literal-name`).

## Proposal
- Resolve directory import specifiers to `index.{ts,js}` (TypeScript module resolution), within the same bounds.
- Follow `export * from` one level when exactly one star-exported module declares the imported name. Ambiguity (several star exports declaring it) reads UNKNOWN with the candidate paths.
- Make the `not-read-whole` unknown say which hop failed (directory index, star export, non-literal member, other).

## Acceptance criteria
- A fixture with exactly the shape above resolves every state name and parent through the enum.
- A fixture with two star exports declaring the same name reads UNKNOWN `ambiguous-reexport` with both paths.
- Existing #685/#705 fixtures compile to the same bytes.
